- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.75) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) or shows sharp reversal, especially after recent peaks.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — model tends to overreact and peak too high, then corrects downward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in such cases.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is bullish; adjust downward by 2–5% for first 7 days if sentiment >0.7.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 3–5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Avoid overconfidence in “trending” sentiment — if sentiment is high but recent price action shows divergence (e.g., rising sentiment with falling price), reduce forecast by 5–10%.
